schedule.schedule:
This is a model-only result. Nothing talked to the robot, nothing was flashed, and nothing was written to the repos.

Margins used. Every point of the tibia, femur and knee actuator outlines is checked, and each limit must hold in the worst of 334 ensemble members:
- Ensemble members: the yaw-0 refit (called "primary" below, because yaw 0 puts the leg furthest inboard), the nominal fit, 32 corners and 300 random members.
- Ensemble spread: true yaw 0-40; femur and knee maps ±2 deg each; L_toe ±0.75 in; pivot ±0.25 in; compliance 0 to +2 deg; floor height ±0.5 in.
- Belly gap must be at least 0. The contact facts are only touch / no touch, and the model already touches 0-15 counts early, so there is no extra gap. The planning target for the bottleneck is at least 1 in.
- Table: any part below the table top must stay at x >= -10. That is the 13.75 in edge, minus 2 in for the robot sitting off-centre, minus 1.75 in of margin (the geom2 rule). The actual edge (x >= -13.75) is reported alongside.
- Floor: at least 3 in above the floor, which allows for the mat over gravel and the rounded toe.

Grid is 8 counts; the chosen moves were rechecked at 1-2 counts over all members.

Q1, solid-table reach. One joint at a time from (0,0), the furthest hip in the worst case is 912 counts, and only with a knee staircase (0 -> 896 at knee 296, knee to 312, -> 912), at a bottleneck of +0.08 in. With one knee value the furthest is 904 at knee 296 (+0.23 in). No cell is feasible at hip 920 or beyond, at any knee.
- The primary model on its own reaches 968.
- Using the actual edge with no off-centre margin, the worst case reaches 992 by tucking the knee at 56 between the belly and the edge (belly 0.38 in, edge 0.17 in). That is too tight to use.
- The 1069 extend switch is not reachable. What blocks it, by knee band (worst case):
  - -17 to 0: belly (the folded tibia, as measured at 941-1003).
  - 8 to 40: belly, plus the 10 in table rule.
  - 48 to 96: belly, plus the table edge.
  - 104 to 384: table edge only. The tibia lies inboard below the top, and the toe ends 4-7.4 in past the edge at z -6 to -10, like pose D.
  - 392 to 584: table edge plus floor.
  - 592 to 656: table rule plus floor.
  - 664 to 785: floor. The tibia points down, and the toe would be up to 18 in past the floor margin.
- In the primary model the knee-80 point sits exactly between belly and edge with about 0.3-0.6 in on each side. That is not credible as a safe pose.

Q2, recommended schedule: K = 264, H = 864.

| Move | Worst-case bottleneck | Primary | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| M1: hip 0, knee curls to its stop (over-curl down to -17 allowed) | +2.10 in, femur belly gap, constant at hip 0 | +2.83 in | Table +11.0, floor +14.7 |
| M2: hip 0, knee uncurls -17 -> 785 switch | +2.10 in | +2.83 in | Any knee overshoot is safe at hip 0 |
| M3: hip 0, knee 785 -> 264 | +2.10 in | | Overshoot tolerance over 250 counts |
| M4: knee 264, hip 0 -> 864 | +1.73 in, table rule at hip 864 (tibia toe at x -8.3 worst, -5.8 primary; table edge 5.48 in away) | Table +4.07, floor +4.75 | Belly +2.10. Floor +2.47 in at hip 739, mid-sweep, where the tibia hangs nearly vertical |

Tolerances for M4:
- Hip overshoot: 27 counts past 864 (stops at 891, table rule, tibia).
- Knee held during the sweep: 224-304 keeps the worst case at 0 or above. The low side is the table at H (+0.48 at 224). The high side is the floor around hip 764 (0.00 at 304). That is ±40 counts, against the knee's 5-9 count spring-back.
- Knee drift once parked at H: down to 216 is fine (+0.27); upward it fails at 312 (-0.30, floor).

Alternatives, if more hip is worth less margin:
- K 272, H 880: +1.00 in (floor +1.97 at hip 781), hip overshoot 15 counts.
- K 296, H 904: +0.23 in, hip overshoot 3 counts.
- The staircase to 912: +0.08 in.

An extra knee move at an intermediate hip gains only 8-16 counts, at bottlenecks below 1 in, so I don't recommend it.

Stand envelope for jogging or T commands (worst case, at least 0, grid): any knee up to hip 560. Knee <= 392 from 568, falling to <= 304 at 688. Knee 112-304 at 832, 208-304 at 864, 296-312 at 904, nothing at 920 or above. The envelope that keeps at least 1 in of margin is in envelope.json.
schedule.return_path:
Return by reversing M4: with the knee held at 264, drive the hip 864 -> 0 until it hits the curl switch. Then the knee is free at hip 0 (park or curl).

The margins are the same cells as the forward sweep. The worst case is +1.73 in at the start (table rule at 864), floor +2.47 at hip 739, belly +2.10 at hip 0. Overshoot at the end is safe, because hip 0 is a switch and any knee is safe at hip 0.

No better path exists. The bottleneck sits at the end pose itself, and the only way out of the narrow window above hip 840 is back along the same knee column. Moving the knee at H first only cuts the margin: it hits 0 at knee 216 or 304, which is +0.27 / -0.30 in.

Rules for the return:
- Do not move the knee until the hip is back below 560. Above that the window closes in on 224-304.
- Use the arrival at the curl switch as a re-home check. The count should be 0 within a few counts; if not, report lost counts.

For the hollow-table full sweep, the return is also the reverse at the same knee. Every pose in it was cleared on this hollow table, and the margins are as in Q4.
schedule.worst_margins:
All values are inches, worst case over the ensemble, with primary (yaw-0 refit) and nominal after the slash.

M1-M3 (hip 0, any knee from -17 to 785):
- Belly +2.10 (femur, knee-independent) / +2.83 / +2.66.
- Table rule +11.0 / +12.9; table edge +14.8; floor +14.7 / +16.9.

M4 and R1 (knee 264, hip 0-864):
- Belly +2.10 at hip 0 (femur) / +2.83.
- Table rule +1.73 at hip 864 (tibia toe) / +4.07 / +4.34. This is the bottleneck.
- Table edge +5.48 / +7.82 / +8.09.
- Floor +2.47 at hip 739 (tibia) / +4.75 / +4.51.
- Hip overshoot tolerance 27 counts; knee band 224-304.
- The member that binds the table is the corner with femur -2, knee -2, L +0.75, yaw 0. The floor is bound by the corners with knee +2, L +0.75, yaw 0.

Q1 limits:
- Staircase to 912: +0.08 (floor at 896, knee 312), table +0.23 at 912.
- Single knee 296 to 904: +0.23 (table at 904), floor +0.49 at hip 756.
- Knee-56 tuck to 990 (actual-edge rule): belly +0.38, edge +0.17, table rule -3.58.

At hip 1069, the best any knee manages in the worst case:
- Knee 120-785: belly +1.18 (femur).
- Knee 280-312: table edge about -7.4.
- Knee 785: floor -18.4.
- No knee clears belly, table and floor together.
schedule.this_table_full_sweep:
On this hollow table, the best knee for a full 0-1069 hip sweep is 192. It is the knee that maximises the smaller of the tibia-belly gap and the floor gap.

Margins at knee 192, fine check (worst / primary / nominal):
- The belly bottleneck is the femur at 1069: +1.18 / +1.57 / +1.44. It does not depend on the knee, and the real sweeps cleared it.
- Tibia to belly: at least +6.86 worst (at 1069).
- Floor: +7.06 worst at hip 650, which is about 10 in above the floor once the 3 in gap is added; +9.13 primary.

Usable knee band: 136-256 keeps the tibia at least 2.4 in from the belly and the floor margin at least 3 in. The measured 157-175 sits inside it. At 157 the tibia-belly gap is +3.6 worst and the floor +7.5. At 184: tibia +6.2, floor +7.6.

On a solid table, knee 192 violates only the table:
- The 10 in rule is crossed at hip 859 worst / 900 primary / 908 nominal.
- The tibia passes the actual edge (x -13.75, below the top) at hip 938 worst / 976 primary / 986 nominal.
- At hip 1069 the toe is at about (-17.8, -9.2) in the primary model. That is 6.1 in (worst) / 4.1 / 3.5 in inside the footprint, about 9 in below the top.
- So the toe would strike the table's side face at hip 940-985, with the whole last 85-130 counts of the stroke inside the table.
- Belly and floor are clear throughout.

Knee 157 behaves the same way: toe at (-16.7, -6.3), 5.1 / 3.1 in inside the edge.
schedule.firmware_notes:
1. Hip extend limit on a solid table.
- Never seek the extend switch, and never use current or stall end-detection on the hip extend during calibration. Any extend stall on the stand is a collision.
- Home the hip on the curl switch (count 0).
- Set the extend limit by arithmetic: HIP_MAX = home + HIP_STROKE_COUNTS, where HIP_STROKE_COUNTS = 1069. That is the FL switch-to-switch count measured on the hollow table, and it agrees with 203.2 mm x 5.26 counts/mm = 1068.8.
- Prefer the measured count to mm x counts/mm. The ruler scale of 5.34-5.44 counts/mm would give 1085-1106 counts.
- Store it per leg. Where a leg's own stroke was measured on the hollow table, use that; otherwise use the default 1069.
- Keep a soft limit about 10 counts short of 1069, so the switch stays a hardware backstop.
- Mark the extend end as "derived, not switch-verified" in EEPROM and telemetry.
- If the extend switch ever trips below about 1069 minus 20 counts, raise an error for lost counts.

2. The calibration hip sweep.
- Drive by count to H = 864, with the knee first parked at K = 264 at hip 0 and held there.
- This replaces CAL_HIP_SWEEP_EDGES = 700 with the knee curled.
- Fail as "obstacle" on any stall or current rise before H, retract to the curl switch, and do not retry automatically.
- Interlock: refuse to command the hip past 560 unless the knee is homed and reads 224-304. Abort the sweep if the knee leaves that band. The model allows ±40 counts.
- Return by retracting the hip to the curl switch with the knee still at K, and check that the re-home count is about 0. Move the knee only once the hip is below 560.

3. Knee values.
- KNEE_CURL_STOP = 0 (mechanical). Over-curl to -17 is safe at hip 0.
- KNEE_SWITCH = 785.
- K_CAL_SOLID = 264, tolerance 224-304.
- Optional longer sweeps: K 272 to H 880 (+1.0 in margin), or K 296 to H 904 (+0.23 in, too tight).
- K_HOLLOW_FULL_SWEEP = 192 (band 136-256), only on this garage table and only with an explicit owner opt-in for a "hollow stand".

4. Runtime stand envelope for T and jog (worst case, at least 0):
- Up to hip 560: any knee.
- Hip 568-680: knee <= 392 tapering to 312.
- Hip 688-824: knee <= 304.
- Hip 832-864: knee about 112-304 narrowing to 208-304.
- Hip above 864: refuse on the stand.
- Table-and-floor margins of at least 1 in shrink these windows; envelope.json has both.

5. Caveats.
- Only the FL leg is modelled. Other legs need their own femur and knee maps before using these counts.
- The hip plate outline (MEAS p2) and the knee actuator size are guesses, but the bindings above are the tibia toe and the femur, not those parts.
- Verify H and K on FL with clearance_sweep.py under supervision before flashing.

schedule.summary:
The hip's extend switch (1069 counts) cannot be reached on a solid table at any knee setting, so calibration should not try to reach it. The recommended schedule is knee 264 and hip 864. Everything here is from the FL leg model only; nothing ran on the robot.

**Reach on a solid table:** the furthest the hip can safely go, worst case over the whole ensemble, is 912 counts. That needs one extra knee move partway out, and the margin is only 0.08 in. With a single knee value the limit is 904 (knee 296). What blocks 1069 depends on the knee:
- knee 104-384: the table edge;
- curled knee: the belly;
- uncurled knee: the floor;
- in between: two of these at once.

**Recommended schedule:**
1. At hip 0, curl the knee to its stop, uncurl it to the switch (785), then set it to 264. Everything at hip 0 is clear by at least 2.1 in.
2. With the knee held at 264, drive the hip from 0 to 864.
   - The tightest point is the toe at hip 864, 1.73 in from the 10 in table limit (5.5 in from the real edge).
   - Halfway out (hip 739) the toe is 2.47 in above the 3 in floor allowance.
   - The hip can overshoot 864 by 27 counts, and the knee can sit anywhere from 224 to 304 during the sweep.
3. Return by reversing: hip back to its curl switch with the knee still at 264, then check the count reads about 0. No other return path is better.

**This hollow table:** knee 192 is best for a full 0-1069 sweep. The tibia stays at least 6.9 in from the belly and the floor margin is at least 7 in (worst case). On a solid table that sweep would break only the table rule: the toe passes the real edge at hip 938-986 and ends 3.5-6.1 in inside the table at 1069, about 9 in below the top.

**Firmware:** home the hip on its curl switch and set the extend limit to home + 1069 counts (the stroke measured switch to switch), marked as not checked by the switch. Sweep the hip by count to 864 with the knee held at 264 (allowed 224-304). Treat any stall before 864 as an obstacle and retract. Calibration knee values are 0 (curl stop), 785 (switch), 264 (solid table) and 192 (hollow table only).

Everything is in C:/Users/nickm/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/78c86551260afdf9/720ce176-f876-4a62-9959-4e2b88a4d5da/scratchpad/geom3/schedule/; schedule_result.json has the headline numbers.

check.disagreements:
No sign or geometry error found in the schedule, but six points need correcting or caveating before it goes into firmware.

1. **Knee sign in the firmware notes.** The firmware's encoder frame is extend-positive (`firmware/arduino/actuator_manager.h` lines 22-33): hip limits are [0, N], knee limits are [-S, 0]. The hip numbers (home 0, H = 864, HIP_MAX = home + 1069) are right as written. The knee numbers are "counts uncurled from the curl stop", so in the firmware frame they are negative:
   - K = 264 is x = -264, and the switch at 785 is -785.
   - The 224-304 interlock is [-304, -224].
   - "Over-curl to -17" is +17.
   Written as positive firmware constants they would be wrong.

2. **The margins are the optimistic end of a range.** The model stage's toe length is 31.79 ± 0.75 in (ruler fit), so its longest tibia is the CAD 32.5 in with nothing above it. Its knee map is one curve ± 2 deg, though the readings at 157 (40-48.5) and 296 (62.6-72) spread wider. The K 264 / H 864 worst case under three assumption sets:

   | Assumptions | Table rule at 864 | Floor allowance | Hip overshoot |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | Stage's own | +2.00 | +2.10 (hip 726) | 30 counts |
   | Plus knee-map spread | +1.57 | +1.01 | 24 counts |
   | Plus toe up to 33.25 in | +0.88 | +0.46 | 14 counts |

   With femur ± 4 deg as well, the table rule is -0.01. In every case the real table edge is at least 3.7 in away and the toe at least 3.4 in above the floor.

3. **The 224-304 knee interlock is too wide at the top.** My worst case over the sweep goes negative above about 292 with the stage's own assumptions (-0.54 in at 304, floor allowance), above 280 with the knee-map spread, and above 272 with the longer toe. The low side holds to 208, 216 and 244 respectively. Use about 244-280 (K ± 16-20), still well outside the 5-9 count spring-back. This eats allowance, not a collision: the toe stays at least 1.3 in off the floor at 304.

4. **h_max 912 is a knife-edge.** I get 912 (single knee 904-910) only with the stage's assumptions. The stated staircase (0 to 896 at knee 296, knee to 312, on to 912) misses the 3 in floor allowance by 0.04-0.58 in in my model. With the wider knee spread or toe up to 33.25 in, h_max is 888-896. Quote it as about 890-910; it does not change the recommendation.

5. **Hollow-table knee band 136-256 is too low at the bottom.** At knee 136 my worst tibia-to-belly gap at hip 1069 is +1.5 in (+0.25 with the wider set), not the 2.4 in or more claimed. At 104-120 it can touch. Use about 157-232. Knee 192 itself is fine.

6. **Weak validation and wording.**
   - The contact check is weaker than stated. Both rigid models put first tibia-belly touch earlier for a tighter curl (mine: 914 at knee 0, 963 at knee 24). The firmware comment records the opposite: a stop at 1003 curled tight and 941 at knee 24. Those are PWM-80 stall points after pressing, so only "touch happens before the stop" is confirmed. This affects the curled-knee side of the envelope, not K = 264, which is at least 14 in from the belly.
   - "Femur belly gap +2.10 / +1.18" is not a moving-part clearance. It is the femur root next to the hub and depends on how much hub is excluded (0.5 in with none, 2.1 with 2.6 in, 4.7 with 4.5 in). Hip 0 is safe because nothing touched there on the robot.
   - "Floor +2.47 at hip 739, where the tibia hangs nearly vertical" is a wrong description: the tibia is about 45 deg off vertical there. The number is about right (mine +2.10 at hip 726).
   - The knee-56 tuck to 990 touches the belly in my worst case (-0.5 in). The stage already calls it unusable.
check.summary:
I agree with the schedule stage: the extend switch is unreachable on a solid table, and knee 264 / hip 864 with a reversed return is safe, though its margins are thinner than quoted under wider assumptions. This is a model-only check; nothing touched the robot, the repos or git.

**How I checked.** I rebuilt the kinematics from `geom3_inputs.md` and `k1_knee_angles.md` without reading the model or schedule code. Every move was checked at every count over the tibia and femur outlines and a guessed knee-actuator envelope. The ensemble was yaw 0-40, femur ± 2 (and ± 4), knee ± 2 on four map variants, toe 31.75-33.25 in, pivot ± 0.25 and floor ± 0.5. Margins are the stage's: body gap at least 0, parts below the table top at x >= -10, and 3 in above the floor.

**Model sanity.** Ruler poses A-D reproduce within 1-2 in. The knee 157-175 full sweep clears the belly in every member, and hip 0 is clear at any knee.

- **Solid-table reach: agree.** 1069 is infeasible in every member, including the nominal alone. No knee clears belly, table and floor together; knee 104-384 ends 4.5-7.7 in inside the table footprint.
- **h_max: agree, loosely.** I reproduce 912 (single knee 904-910) with the stage's assumptions, and 888-896 with wider ones. Treat it as about 890-910 and unusable.
- **M1-M3 (hip 0, knee -17 to 785): agree.** Tibia to body is at least 4.4 in, the table rule at least 9.5 and the floor at least 13.2.
- **M4 (knee 264, hip 0 to 864): agree it is safe.** With the stage's assumptions I get table rule +2.00 at 864 (stage +1.73), real edge +5.75 (stage +5.48) and floor +2.10 at hip 726 (stage +2.47 at 739). The binding corner is the same: femur -2, knee -2, longest toe, yaw 0. Wider assumptions cut this to +0.9 / +0.5, but the real edge stays at least 3.7 in away. K = 264 is at or within 8 counts of my best K for H = 864.
- **Return path: agree.** Reversing M4 uses the same cells, and "any knee is safe up to hip 560" reproduces exactly (536 with a toe up to 33.25 in).
- **Hollow-table sweep at knee 192: agree.** Tibia to belly is at least +4.8 to +6.2 in and the floor margin at least +4.5 to +7.4. On a solid table the 10 in rule is crossed at about hip 858 (nominal 883) and the real edge at about 941 (nominal 959). At 1069 the leg is 4.7 in (nominal) to 5.6 in (worst) inside the table.

**Changes I recommend:** write the knee constants with the firmware's negative sign, narrow the knee interlock to about 244-280, raise the hollow-table band's low end to about 157, and quote the M4 margin as roughly +0.9 to +2.0 in. Details are in the disagreements field.

model_summary:
Built leg_model_v3.py, a forward-kinematics model of the FL leg. Hip counts drive the femur angle and knee counts drive the knee angle, each through a smooth monotone cubic fitted to the MEASURED tables; no hip or knee linkage is used. A third input is the yaw. The model returns the outlines of the femur (CAD), knee actuator (capsule), tibia (CAD, taper about 4.9 deg) and toe (rounded end plus tip point) in the wall frame. The fixed geometry is pivot (3.0, 2.5) and femur 23.0 in, and the tibia direction is 180 + femur + knee interior.

The fit is done jointly by scipy least squares. Both cubics, the toe length, the ruler yaw and the pivot are fitted against all femur and knee readings (within their error bars), ruler poses A-D (1 in sigma), and priors on the pivot (±0.25 in) and toe length.

Main numbers:
- Toe length 31.8 in.
- Ruler yaw 18 deg, but the data accept anything from 0 to 30, so a yaw-0 refit is kept as well.
- Femur angle 40.7 / 8.3 / -30.4 / -65.8 at hip 0 / 478 / 846 / 1069.
- Knee interior angle 19.5 / 43.5 / 66 / 99 / 113 / 124 / 132 at knee 0 / 157 / 296 / 508 / 608 / 706 / 785.
- Every measured point is within its error bar except ruler B z (1.04 in) and one of the two disagreeing readings at knee 296.

All contact facts are reproduced:
- Belly contact with the knee curled starts at hip 928-980 for knee 0-24, at most about 2 deg earlier than the measured 941-1003, which is the safe direction.
- Knee 157-175 clears the full sweep, with the tibia at least 5.7 in from the body.
- Hip 0 is clear for every knee setting.
- Pose D's toe is 16 in under the body and 2.3-3.0 in inside the table footprint.

Corridor margins in clearances() (positive means clear):
- Body: distance from the body box minus 0. A planner adds its own margin; the femur hub inside 3 in of the pivot is left out.
- Table: anything below the table top must stay at x >= -10, the geom2 rule of 13.75 minus 2 in off-centre minus 1.75 in margin. The raw distance to the table edge is also reported as table_contact.
- Floor: z >= floor + 3 in, because the floor is a mat over gravel, its height is ±0.5 in and the toe is rounded.
- The worst plywood face toward the body is used, shifted by 0.5 x sin(yaw).

Ensemble generator, ensemble(n, seed):
- Femur map: offsets U[-2, 2] deg at hip 0 and 1069, linear in between.
- Knee map: offsets U[-2, 2] deg at knee 0 and 785, linear in between.
- Compliance U[0, +2] deg.
- Pivot ±0.25 in on each axis.
- Toe length ±0.75 in.
- True yaw U[0, 40] deg.
- Floor ±0.5 in.
- It also includes the 32 corners and the nominal fit. Each member carries ruler chi2 under both readings of the side measurements and its contact-fact pass/fail. In the random members, first contact at knee 0 falls at 897-963 (5th-95th percentile), and the knee 157-175 sweep is clear in every member.

Other entry points: leg_outlines, toe_tip, clearances, first_belly_contact, femur_elev_deg, knee_interior_deg and their inverses, validation, contact_checks, ensemble. Nothing touched the robot, git, or the repos.
